items.title: Recycled wool chore coat, slate blue

listing.seller: Kettle Hill Workroom Demo (SIMULATED), workroom since 2012
listing.text:
Recycled wool chore coat in slate blue: three patch pockets, corozo buttons and a straight, boxy cut. Made in sizes XS to XL.

How we started. Kettle Hill began at a single rented cutting table in a garment factory in Kwai Chung. The two of us who started it had spent years drafting patterns for other labels, and when the factory moved most of its lines away, a few tables stayed behind. That first year we made aprons for cafes and repaired uniforms for a hotel laundry, which taught us more about seams that last than any course could. The chore coat came later, when a regular customer brought in a jacket her grandfather had worn on the docks and asked whether we could make another one like it. We could not copy it exactly, but we studied how it had aged: where the elbows had thinned, which pocket corners had torn, how the collar had softened. Every detail of this coat comes from that afternoon.

Who makes it. We are now a team of nine. We still cut by hand in small runs of around sixty coats, and each coat is sewn from start to finish by one machinist instead of being passed down a line. That is slower, and it is part of why the coat costs what it does, but it means the person who sets the sleeves is the same person who checks the buttonholes at the end. Inside the left pocket there is a small label with the initials of whoever made yours.

The cloth. The fabric is woven from reclaimed wool fibres blended with a smaller share of new wool for strength. It comes from a family mill in northern Italy that has been reclaiming wool from old knitwear and tailoring offcuts for several generations. Garments are sorted by colour before they are broken down, so the slate blue you see is mostly the colour of the sweaters and jackets it came from, and very little new dye is needed. Because the fibres have been spun once already, they are shorter than virgin wool, which gives the cloth a soft, slightly felted handle and a little texture on the surface. The weave is a tight twill that sheds light drizzle and resists snagging. The buttons are corozo, the hard seed of a tropical palm, and the pocket linings are undyed cotton twill left over from our apron orders.

Fit. The coat is cut to sit over a shirt or a light knit rather than a thick hoodie, so go up one size if you like to layer heavily. The sleeves are a touch long so you can turn them back once. The shoulders are unpadded, and a small box pleat at the back gives you room to reach forward without the coat pulling across the chest. A medium weighs a little under a kilo, which feels substantial on the hanger and surprisingly light once it is on.

Care. Wool cleans itself more than most people expect. After a day's wear, hang the coat on a broad wooden hanger somewhere airy and most smells will be gone by morning. Every few weeks, brush it downward with a clothes brush to lift dust before it settles into the weave. Dab small marks with a damp cloth and a drop of wool detergent instead of rubbing them. When it needs a proper clean, take it to a dry cleaner you trust, or hand wash it in cool water, press the water out in a towel and dry it flat out of direct sun. Never wring it, and keep it out of the tumble dryer. Steam out creases; if you must iron, use a pressing cloth on the wool setting. Between seasons, store it clean in a breathable cotton cover with a cedar block, because moths go for worn, unwashed wool.

Repairs and returns. We repair our own coats free of charge for as long as you own them, whether that means a loose button, a torn pocket corner or a frayed cuff. If the coat is not right for you, send it back unworn within 30 days for a full refund. Delivery within Hong Kong is free and usually takes three working days. Questions about sizing or the cloth are welcome through the contact form on this page, and one of the makers will reply.

listing.seller: Commute Cloth Co Demo (SIMULATED), shop since 2016
listing.text:
Stretch twill commuter trousers in navy with a slim straight leg, waist 28 to 40. Below are the questions customers ask us most often.

How do I find my size? Measure around your natural waist, just above the hip bones, with a soft tape held level and snug but not tight. Compare that figure with the waist column in the size chart. If you fall between two sizes, choose the larger one: the waistband has some give, but the seat does not.

Do they run small or large? True to size in the waist and slightly slim through the thigh. Customers with athletic legs often take one size up and have a tailor take in the waist, which costs much less than letting out a seat.

Which leg lengths are there? Short, regular and long, finishing at about seventy-six, eighty-one and eighty-six centimetres. There is extra fabric folded inside the hem, so a tailor can let them down by around three centimetres.

What is the fabric made of? A cotton-rich twill with a small amount of elastane, woven tightly enough to keep its colour and shape through a working week. The inside has a soft brushed finish, so it does not feel cold in air conditioning.

Will they shrink? The twill is washed before cutting, so shrinkage should stay under one percent if you follow the care label. Hot washes and tumble drying are what usually make trousers shorter, so keep to thirty degrees and line dry.

Will the navy fade? The yarn is dyed before it is woven, so the colour holds well. Washing them inside out and drying them away from strong sun slows any fading even further.

Is the stretch noticeable? Two percent elastane gives enough movement for cycling or taking stairs two at a time, without the fabric looking shiny or bagging at the knee by evening.

Do the pockets hold a phone? Yes. The front pockets are deep enough for a large phone, and the back right pocket has a hidden button so a wallet stays put on a crowded commute.

How fast is delivery? Orders confirmed before four in the afternoon on a working day are packed that day. Courier delivery usually takes one to three working days, and a tracking email follows as soon as the parcel leaves us.

Can I collect instead? Yes. At checkout, pick a self-service locker or a pickup counter at a convenience store near you. We text you when the parcel is ready, and it waits there for three days.

Do you deliver to the outlying islands? We do, at no extra cost, though it can take an extra working day or two.

What happens if I miss the courier? The courier tries again the next working day. After a second missed attempt the parcel goes to a nearby pickup point and we email you the address.

How do returns work? You have thirty days from delivery to send back unworn trousers with the tags still on. Request a return label through the link in your delivery email, stick it over the old one, and hand the parcel to any courier counter. Your first return on each order costs nothing.

Can I order two sizes and return one? You can. Plenty of customers order neighbouring waist sizes, keep the pair that fits and send the other back under that same free return.

When will I get my money back? We check each return within two working days of it arriving. Once it passes, we release the refund to the card or account you paid with; most banks show it within a week.

Can I swap for another size? Yes, at no charge. Choose exchange rather than refund when you request the label, and we will set the new size aside at once so it cannot sell out while your parcel is in transit.

What if a seam fails? Tell us within a year of purchase, with a picture of the problem, and we will mend the trousers or send a new pair. That applies to sale purchases too.

Is there a matching jacket? Not yet. We are testing a jacket in the same twill and will list it on this page when it is ready.
